title: Sgt. Weaver at the scheduling boards
description: Sgt. Weaver — an ex-Marine, Larry says — leans on the quarter-hour flight-scheduling racks inside the pegboard-walled operations van, cigarette in hand, whistle cord around his neck. The boards behind him carry stenciled time blocks and a ruled status chart; a shield-shaped patch is stitched at his left pocket. Weaver, Larry says, "was a cool guy and hung out with me a lot."
researchNotes: Larry's own identification (Memories comment, 2026-08-15; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0014-c18032226.json). The survey had independently read this man's name tape as beginning 'WE...' — testimony and the machine reading converge on WEAVER. Weaver is also the sergeant (an E5) who responded to the bathroom shooting in Larry's fuller 2026-08-15 account (data/recollections/giscus-stories-c18035411.json). Magnification pass 2026-08-15 (research/magnification/vn-0014-pocket-patch.png): the patch shows a bird-form center over two lines of red lettering, but the letters sit below this scan's resolution — the full reading now waits on a high-resolution re-scan of the original slide. 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0014-c18415711.json), with 'Location: Ton Son Nhut': inside the van; the day shift 'probably 4 guys' and the night shift one; Larry on nights a lot 'because I was going to the mountain a lot in Nui Ba Den. I felt safer on the mountain that I did at Ton Son Nhut.' This agrees with the twelve-hour night shifts alone of VN-0015 and gives a reason for them — a man rotating to the mountain took the single-man shift at the base.
